about.title: Lathrop Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Lathrop has grown quickly, and many residents now rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and larger San Joaquin County hospital systems for treatment. Most visits go fine, but when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the consequences can follow someone for years. California law recognizes that patients deserve care that meets an accepted medical standard, and when it doesn't, injured patients have options — though a poor result by itself isn't proof of malpractice. Medical malpractice cases are technical: they require medical records, expert review, and strict attention to deadlines under California's MICRA rules. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee itself; we simply help Lathrop residents connect with an independent, contingency-fee attorney who can evaluate whether what happened meets the legal definition of malpractice and explain next steps in plain language.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Documentation Matter in Lathrop

items.title: Short, Strict Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Waiting even a few months to look into what happened can put a claim at risk.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice. An attorney familiar with this process can help make sure Lathrop-area claims are set up correctly from the start.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't establish malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically must review the case and confirm the care fell below an accepted standard. Connecting early with an attorney helps get that review moving.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Lathrop?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines are strict and can be easy to miscalculate, it helps to have them reviewed early.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or disappointing result means a provider did something wrong. Malpractice requires showing the care fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done, which is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records.

items.question: Do I have to go to a hospital in Lathrop specifically to have a claim?
items.answer: No — the claim depends on where and how the care was provided, not simply your home address. Many Lathrop residents receive care at facilities throughout San Joaquin County, and an attorney can help sort out which providers and records are relevant regardless of the specific location.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything or represent me directly?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't charge any fee. We simply help match you with an independent attorney in our network who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
